The topic of from the angle came up in today's meeting.
I want to ring, press? right now.
How about trying to ring, press? together tomorrow?

meanings.en: to film, to shoot, to take (a photo)
meanings.note: Used for capturing photos or video.
Also means to stamp a seal or dip food into sauce.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
May I take a photo here?

examples.text: 신디 씨는 일반적으로 알려진 얼짱 각도에서 눌러 찍기보다는 왼쪽 프로필 라인이 좀 더 살거든요.
examples.trans: Rather than shooting downward from the standard selfie angle, your left profile line comes alive much better.
The topic of left side came up in today's meeting.

examples.text: 신디 씨는 일반적으로 알려진 얼짱 각도에서 눌러 찍기보다는 왼쪽 프로필 라인이 좀 더 살거든요.
examples.trans: Rather than shooting downward from the standard selfie angle, your left profile line comes alive much better.
The topic of side profile came up in today's meeting.

examples.text: 신디 씨는 일반적으로 알려진 얼짱 각도에서 눌러 찍기보다는 왼쪽 프로필 라인이 좀 더 살거든요.
examples.trans: Rather than shooting downward from the standard selfie angle, your left profile line comes alive much better.
The topic of profile line came up in today's meeting.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

meanings.note: Past tense is 샀다 / 샀어요.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the mart.
I need to buy a birthday present for my friend.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: colloquially often pronounced/written 이쁘다

examples.trans: The flowers are really pretty.
This color is prettier.
I want to making right now.
How about trying to making together tomorrow?
I want to stayed up all night right now.
How about trying to stayed up all night together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this face, though?
I was busy today because of face, though.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 그래야 좋은 그림이 나와. 너 신디 매력이 뭐냐?
examples.trans: That is the only way great footage comes out. Tell me, what is Cindy's charm?

examples.text: 이거 봐, 네가 찍어온 출연자 매력도 못 보면서 무슨 예고를 만들어? 네가 못 보는 걸 다른 사람들은 볼 수 있겠니?
examples.trans: Look at you—how can you cut a preview when you cannot even see the charm of the cast member you filmed? How will viewers see what you cannot?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그럼 문제 없네, 이거 살려, 신디 표정도 살리고.
examples.trans: Then there is no problem—keep this cut in, and keep Cindy's expression too.
This expression comes from 'keep it in'.

meanings.note: Used as noun + topic (포인트는).

examples.text: 놀이공원 측에서 연락 왔는데요, 야외 취침할 장소 포인트는 직접 보셨으면 하던데요.
examples.trans: The amusement park contacted us—they hoped you would inspect the outdoor sleeping spot in person.
This point about exact spot is really important.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

examples.text: 지난번도 느낀 건데 너 누구한테 연애를 가르치니?
examples.trans: I noticed this last time too—who do you think you are lecturing about romance?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 느끼다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (felt, noticed).

meanings.note: Used when reading decimal numbers, e.g. 오 점 칠 (5.7).

examples.text: 이번 주 시청률은 오 점 칠이에요.
examples.trans: This week's ratings are five point seven.
I learned many good points.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'main', used before nouns like 피디 ('PD') or 요리 ('dish').

examples.trans: Today's main dish is steak.
That person is the main writer of this program.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'camera'

examples.trans: Please move the camera over here.
I bought a new camera.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 비 오는데 야외 취침하라고 했어 봐, 너네 다 돌았냐고!
examples.trans: Imagine telling them to sleep outdoors in the rain—they would ask if we had all lost our minds!
This expression comes from 'have you gone crazy!'.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

examples.text: 보고 나서 느낀 점은 신디 씨는 메인 카메라가 돌지 않거나 거울을 보고 있지 않을 때 훨씬 더 예쁘다는 겁니다, 지금처럼.
examples.trans: What I realized afterward is that you look far prettier when the main camera is not rolling and you are not looking in a mirror—like right now.

examples.text: 의자, 내 앞에 놓으면 어떡해? 거울 앞에 놔야지.
examples.trans: That chair—why put it in front of me? Put it in front of the mirror.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2
I understand well (far, much).
Today is a (far, much) busy day.

meanings.note: 르-irregular adjective; conjugates as 달라요 in polite present.
In its adnominal form 다른, modifies a following noun to mean 'other' or 'another'.

examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?
Our thoughts are different from each other.

examples.text: 너 지금 경합이 무슨 뜻인지 알고 그런 소리 하니?
examples.trans: Do you even know what competition means when you say that?
The topic of what meaning it is came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

examples.text: 다른 뜻이 있는 건 아니고요, 피디로서 그렇게 분석을 해봤다는 거죠. 고생하셨습니다!
examples.trans: I did not mean anything else by it—just that I analyzed it that way as a producer. Thank you for your hard work!
The topic of analysis came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Goodbye, and thank you for your hard work!
This expression comes from 'keep up the hard work!'.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
